content: ## Metadata_Start ## code: en ## title: Events Caching 2.0 ## slug: events-caching-2 ## seoTitle: Caching 2.0 ## description: ## contentType: Markdown ## Metadata_End {{snippet.Caching2_and_EventGrp_Warning}} ## Caching 2.0 Terminology ### Batched Cache Invalidation * *Frequency: 1 minute* * Cache invalidation occurs based on the actions performed in {{variable.Product_Salesforce}}. The path is {{variable.Product_Salesforce}} to cache. * All cache invalidation requests are grouped and processed in batches within one minute. This means that multiple requests are collected and executed together every minute instead of immediately invalidating the cache upon each request. * This system efficiently handles cache invalidation requests, ensuring none are lost, even if multiple requests come in simultaneously. ### Auto Refresh * *Frequency:* * *{{variable.Object_EventGroup}} listing - Five minutes after the previous user visit* * *{{variable.Object_Event}} resources and Data Dictionaries - one hour after first user visit* * Auto refresh serves as a backup mechanism for cache invalidation, providing an additional opportunity to update the cache. * It is triggered when a user visits a URL. As soon as the auto-refresh timing threshold is met for that URL, a refresh job is scheduled. * The auto-refresh threshold for {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} listings is five minutes, meaning that if someone visits the listing after it has been cached for five minutes, a refresh job will be scheduled. The threshold for other resources, like {{variable.Object_Event}}s and Data Dictionaries, is one hour. * Auto-refresh reuses the same jobs as cache invalidation. ### Manual Actions #### Publish Button The {{variable.Field_ETEvent_Publish}} button existed prior to the Caching 2.0 update. * ***Where?*** This button is on the {{variable.Object_Event}}s record page in the top right corner (in the BT Events Publish component). * ***What?*** Use this button to publish new or unpublished {{variable.Object_Event}}s. It behaves similarly to the {{variable.Button_Events_Update}} button, refreshing the {{variable.Object_Event}} and potentially triggering a refresh of the {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} listing. * ***When?*** Use this button to publish a new {{variable.Object_Event}} or to republish an unpublished {{variable.Object_Event}}. Republishing an {{variable.Object_Event}} results in the same cache updates as the {{variable.Button_Events_Update}} button. #### Update Button The {{variable.Button_Events_Update}} button existed before the Caching 2.0 update. * ***Where?*** This button is on the {{variable.Object_Event}}s record page in the top right corner (in the BT Events Publish component, underneath the {{variable.Field_ETEvent_Publish}} button). * ***What?*** When clicked, this button triggers a cache invalidation job that refreshes the {{variable.Object_Event}} within a one-minute batch. It also checks if the {{variable.Object_Event}} is included in its targeted {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} listing. If it isn’t, a new job is scheduled to refresh the {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} listing, ensuring that new {{variable.Object_Event}}s or those moved into new {{variable.Object_EventGroup}}s appear quickly. The entire process takes slightly over two minutes. * ***When?*** * If {{variable.Object_Event}} updates need to be reflected quickly. (It usually happens within two minutes.) * If an {{variable.Object_Event}} needs to be added to a new {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} or moved back to the default {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} listing quickly. (It usually happens within five minutes.) #### Clear the Group Listing Cache Button * ***Where?*** The {{variable.Button_ClearGroupListingCache}} button is on the {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} record page. * ***What?*** Clicking this button causes a reset and is heavier in processing. It refreshes the {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} summaries and removes everything related to the {{variable.Object_EventGroup}}, ensuring a fresh load on the next request. This resource-intensive operation may take several minutes and may lead to higher API calls on {{variable.Product_Salesforce}}'s side and an increased load on the cache on the webapp side. * ***When?*** * If a user makes multiple changes that affect multiple {{variable.Object_Event}}s in an {{variable.Object_EventGroup}}. The update will happen on its own with up to an hour delay, but clicking this button forces the update immediately. #### Update Group Listing Cache Button * ***Where?*** The {{variable.Button_UpdateGroupListingCache}} button is located on the {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} object. * ***What?*** Clicking this button allows users to refresh the {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} summaries or listing, especially when adding/deleting an {{variable.Object_Event}} from the {{variable.Object_EventGroup}}. * ***When?*** * If a user adds or deletes an {{variable.Object_Event}} from an {{variable.Object_EventGroup}}. The update will happen on its own with up to a two minute day, but clicking this button forces the update immediately. ## When Do Cache Updates Happen? :::(Error) (Caution) If you are using the nightly cache refresh job (Schedule Event Cache Refresh), you must turn it off before enabling Caching 2.0. Go to the Blackthorn | Events Admin tab, click the Scheduled Jobs tab, and click the **Disable Event Cache Refresh Job** button. ::: ### Every Minute The following tasks happen every minute once an {{variable.Object_Event}}'s cache invalidation {{variable.Product_Salesforce}} job is complete. * Move an {{variable.Object_Event}} from one {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} to another. The {{variable.Object_Event}} will no be longer visible on the original {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} listing (i.e. not visible in the {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} that it was removed from) * Delete an {{variable.Object_Event}}. * Remove an {{variable.Object_Event}} from an {{variable.Object_EventGroup}}. The {{variable.Object_Event}} will no longer appear on the {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} listing. * Update {{variable.Object_Event}} information, including all {{variable.Object_Event}} fields (i.e, {{variable.Field_ETEvent_EventName}}, dates, {{variable.Field_ETEvent_Description}}). This only includes fields on the {{variable.Object_Event}} object. * Update {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} information (i.e. filter, name, etc.). ### Every Five Minutes The following tasks happen every five minutes after a user visits the page, if the cache was stale when the user visited the page. * Used only with {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} listings. * When a user moves an {{variable.Object_Event}} from one {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} to another, the {{variable.Object_Event}} is visible on the new {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} page. * Manually force an update by performing one of the following actions. * Click {{variable.Button_Events_Update}} on the {{variable.Object_Event}}. * Republish the {{variable.Object_Event}}. * Click the {{variable.Button_UpdateGroupListingCache}} button. ### Every Hour The following tasks fall into this category. * Update a {{variable.Object_DataDictionaryGroup}}. * Update resources related to an {{variable.Object_Event}}, including {{variable.Object_Form}}s, {{variable.Object_Keyword}}s, and {{variable.Object_PaymentGateway}}s. ### Manual Actions The manual actions include clicking the {{variable.Button_Events_Update}} button, republishing an {{variable.Object_Event}}, and refreshing the {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} listing. * Change the {{variable.Object_EventSettings}}. To have the related {{variable.Object_Event}}s reflect the updated values, you must perform one of the following actions. * Republish each {{variable.Object_Event}} related to the Event Settings. * Edit one of the {{variable.Object_Event}}’s fields to trigger an update. * Click the {{variable.Button_Events_Update}} button. * Create a new {{variable.Object_Event}}. To trigger the cache, click {{variable.Button_Events_Publish}}. * Add a new {{variable.Object_Event}} to an already-published {{variable.Object_EventGroup}}. To make the new {{variable.Object_Event}} visible in the {{variable.Object_EventGroup}}, click {{variable.Button_Events_Publish}}. * Clone an {{variable.Object_Event}}. To trigger the cache, click {{variable.Button_Events_Publish}}. * Update {{variable.Object_Form}} fields. To trigger the cache, republish the {{variable.Object_Event}}. * Create a new {{variable.Object_Form}} and add it to an {{variable.Object_Event}}, {{variable.Object_EventItem}}, or {{variable.Object_Session}}. To trigger the cache, republish the related record. ### Other Resolved Issues * {{variable.Object_Event}}s are only visible in the correct {{variable.Object_EventGroup}}s. * When multiple {{variable.Object_Event}}s are updated back-to-back, the changes will appear on the frontend for all updated {{variable.Object_Event}}s. For example, if there are 10 {{variable.Object_Event}}s, all 10 {{variable.Object_Event}}s will be updated, not nine of the 10. ## Use Cases ### Delete an Event * *Frequency: updates every 60 seconds.* * The {{variable.Object_Event}} is removed from the {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} listing once the cache invalidation is completed for the {{variable.Object_Event}} ### Keywords and Event Group URL Filters If Caching 2.0 is enabled and an {{variable.Field_ETGroup_EventGroupURL}} has keywords/filters, both the legacy (pre-Caching 2.0) format ((?keywords=CategoryName:KeywordName) and the new format (?keywords=KeywordName) work as expected. Previously, legacy {{variable.Field_ETGroup_EventGroupURL}} keywords included both the keyword category and keyword in the URL filters, but using them with Caching 2.0 caused empty {{variable.Object_EventGroup}}s. #### Example of Keyword with Caching 2.0 With Caching 2.0 enabled, the {{variable.Object_Keyword}} does not include the {{variable.Field_Keyword_Category}} as a part of the filter URL parameter. * {{variable.Field_Keyword_Keyword}}: School of Business * {{variable.Field_Keyword_Category}}: Department * URL with Caching 2.0 enabled: https://events.blackthorn.io/en/orgId/g/eventGroupId?keywords=School%20of%Businness Result: The URL doesn’t include the “department” category, and the {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} shows the filtered results. #### Example of Keyword with Legacy Cache: * {{variable.Field_Keyword_Keyword}}: School of Business * {{variable.Field_Keyword_Category}}: Department * URL using the legacy cache: https://events.blackthorn.io/en/orgId/g/eventGroupId?keywords=department:School%20of%Businness Result: In this URL, “department:” is included with the Event Group URL filter. The “department:” must be removed from the URL; otherwise, the {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} will appear to have no results if the URL is used directly with Caching 2.0. ### Move an Event from one Event Group to Another * *Frequency: updates when the first visit after five minutes happens* * The {{variable.Object_Event}} is removed from the original {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} once the cache invalidation is complete for the {{variable.Object_Event}} (within 60 seconds). The {{variable.Object_Event}} will then appear in the new {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} listing after any of the following occurs. * A user clicks the {{variable.Button_UpdateGroupListingCache}} button on the new {{variable.Object_EventGroup}}. * A user clicks the {{variable.Button_Events_Update}} button on the {{variable.Object_Event}}. * A user visits the {{variable.Field_ETGroup_EventGroupURL}} after five minutes. (auto-refresh) ### Remove an Event from the Event Group * *Frequency: updates every five minutes* * The {{variable.Object_Event}} is removed from the original {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} listing once the cache invalidation is completed for the {{variable.Object_Event}} (within 60 seconds).. * The {{variable.Object_Event}} appears in the default {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} listing once an auto-refresh occurs for the {{variable.Object_EventGroup}}. ### Set an Event’s Event Group Field * *Frequency: updates every five minutes.* * Set an {{variable.Object_Event}}’s {{variable.Field_ETEvent_EventGroup}} field when the {{variable.Object_Event}} isn’t related to an {{variable.Object_EventGroup}}. * Remove the {{variable.Object_Event}} from the {{variable.Object_EventGroup}}. * The {{variable.Object_Event}} appears/disappears from the {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} listing once an auto-refresh occurs for the {{variable.Object_EventGroup}}. ### Update Event Properties * *Frequency: updates within 60 seconds.* * {{variable.Object_Event}} properties refer to fields on the {{variable.Object_Event}} object, such as {{variable.Field_ETEvent_EventName}} and {{variable.Field_ETEvent_Description}}. * Cache invalidation is triggered automatically on {{variable.Product_Salesforce}}. ### Update Event Item or Event Session Properties * *Frequency: updates within 60 seconds.* * Cache invalidation for these objects is triggered automatically on {{variable.Product_Salesforce}}. * The {{variable.Object_Event}} that the {{variable.Object_EventItem}} or {{variable.Object_Session}} refers to is refreshed automatically. ### Update the Payment Gateway Properties * *Frequency: updates within 60 seconds.* * The {{variable.Object_PaymentGateway}} property updates trigger an automatic cache invalidation on {{variable.Product_Salesforce}}. * The related {{variable.Object_Event}}s need to be refreshed since the number of {{variable.Object_Event}}s could be very large. * The {{variable.Object_PaymentGateway}} is refreshed automatically. * The {{variable.Object_PaymentGateway}} is attached to the {{variable.Object_Event}} dynamically when requested on the webapp, ensuring consistency across all related {{variable.Object_Event}}s in the organization. ### Update Event Settings, Forms, and Other Lookups on the Event * *Frequency: updates with a manual action.* * No cache invalidation is triggered automatically because of the potential for a large number of related {{variable.Object_Event}}s. * The {{variable.Object_EventSettings}}s, {{variable.Object_Form}}s, and other {{variable.Object_Event}} record lookups are updated if a user clicks the {{variable.Button_Events_Update}} button or republishes the {{variable.Object_Event}}. * The {{variable.Object_EventSettings}}s, {{variable.Object_Form}}s, and other {{variable.Object_Event}} record lookups are also updated if a user clicks the {{variable.Button_ClearGroupListingCache}} button. ## FAQ :::(Info) (IMPORTANT) The previous hard refresh actions are no longer supported once you have upgraded to Cache 2.0. ::: **Q: When will caching occur?** A: For most things, the cache will be refreshed within one minute. This includes the following. * Delete an {{variable.Object_Event}}. * Update the {{variable.Object_Event}}, {{variable.Object_EventItem}}, {{variable.Object_Session}}, and {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} fields and related information. * Update the {{variable.Object_PaymentGateway}} fields and related information. The cache will update when the first visit after five minutes happens for the following. * Move an {{variable.Object_Event}} from one {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} to another. * Remove an {{variable.Object_Event}} from an {{variable.Object_EventGroup}}. * Set an {{variable.Object_Event}}’s {{variable.Field_ETEvent_EventGroup}} field when the {{variable.Object_Event}} isn’t related to an {{variable.Object_EventGroup}}. The following tasks can take up to one hour for the cache to refresh. * Update the {{variable.Object_DataDictionaryGroup}}. * Update {{variable.Object_Event}} resources. **Q: How do I refresh the cache immediately?** A: To refresh the cache immediately, click one of the following buttons. * {{variable.Object_Event}} Record * {{variable.Field_ETEvent_Publish}}: Use this button to publish new or unpublished {{variable.Object_Event}}s. It behaves similarly to the {{variable.Button_Events_Update}} button, refreshing the {{variable.Object_Event}} and potentially triggering a refresh of the {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} listing. * {{variable.Button_Events_Update}}: When clicked, this button triggers a cache invalidation job that refreshes the {{variable.Object_Event}} within a one-minute batch. It also checks if the {{variable.Object_Event}} is included in its targeted {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} listing. If it isn’t, a new job is scheduled to refresh the {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} listing, ensuring that new {{variable.Object_Event}}s or those moved into new {{variable.Object_EventGroup}}s appear quickly. The entire process takes slightly over two minutes. * {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} Record * {{variable.Button_UpdateGroupListingCache}}: This button refreshes the {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} summaries, pulling the latest {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} list and updating the Event IDs. (It does not update Event content.) If an {{variable.Object_Event}} was unpublished and republished, it won't be visible until this button is pressed. * {{variable.Button_ClearGroupListingCache}}: This button performs process-heavy actions by refreshing the {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} summaries and marking every {{variable.Object_Event}} in the summaries as stale, ensuring a fresh load on the next request. Despite being resource-intensive, the batch process will occur at one-minute intervals. However, this may lead to higher API calls on {{variable.Product_Salesforce}}'s side and increased Redis load on the webapp side. **Q: I changed a lot of things in an {{variable.Object_EventGroup}}. How do I make the changes visible as quickly as possible?** A: Click the {{variable.Button_ClearGroupListingCache}} button. It will clear the cache related to the {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} including the {{variable.Object_Event}}s in the {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} and reset the {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} listing. **Q: Are there any other ways to update the cache?** A: Yes, you can visit the preview link to force the latest data for an {{variable.Object_Event}} to load. The preview link shares the same cache as the regular link. **Q: I just published an {{variable.Object_Event}} in an {{variable.Object_EventGroup}}, but it’s taking a while to appear there. How does this process work?** A: While a newly published {{variable.Object_Event}} goes live immediately, it may take more than two minutes for it to appear in the related {{variable.Object_EventGroup}}. The time difference is due to several cache refreshes occurring in different parts of the app. If you want the {{variable.Object_Event}} to appear faster, click the {{variable.Button_UpdateGroupListingCache}} button after you use the {{variable.Field_ETEvent_EventPageURL}} to visit the {{variable.Object_Event}}. Updates are processed within one minute. **Q: Should I use the {{variable.Button_UpdateGroupListingCache}} or {{variable.Button_ClearGroupListingCache}} button?** A: Use the {{variable.Button_UpdateGroupListingCache}} button when the only change made to the Event Group was adding or deleting an Event. Use the {{variable.Button_ClearGroupListingCache}} button after updating the Event Group. This button can also be used after adding or deleting Events, but it will temporarily increase load times since a new cache must be created for the Event Group. **Q: How do I add the {{variable.Button_UpdateGroupListingCache}} or {{variable.Button_ClearGroupListingCache}} buttons to the Event Group page layout?** A: Complete the following steps to add the buttons. 1. Click the {{variable.Button_GearIcon}}. 2. Click {{variable.Button_Setup}}. 3. In the Quick Find box, enter and click “Event Group.” 4. Click the Page Layouts tab. 5. Click “Event Group Layout.” 6. In the “Salesforce Mobile and Lightning Experience Actions” section, click **override the predefined actions**. This will allow you to add the buttons. ![Caching_AddButtonEventGroup_1](https://cdn.document360.io/f977eec0-500f-40a3-b663-724a51f78075/Images/Documentation/Caching_AddButtonEventGroup_1.png){height="" width=""} 8. Click the Mobile & Lightning Actions tab. 9. Drag and drop the {{variable.Button_ClearGroupListingCache}} and {{variable.Button_UpdateGroupListingCache}} buttons to the “Salesforce Mobile and Lightning Experience Actions” section. ![Caching_AddButtonEventGroup_2](https://cdn.document360.io/f977eec0-500f-40a3-b663-724a51f78075/Images/Documentation/Caching_AddButtonEventGroup_2.png){height="" width=""} 11. Click {{variable.Button_Save}}.
